newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis sales rise 8 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Novartis sales rise 8 percent in 1996.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals group Novartis AG said Tuesday sales in its core life sciences segment rose by 8 percent in 1996 and that it expected to post a flat full-year profit, excluding one-time items.

The company, formed in December through the merger of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz AG, said group sales rose to 36.23 billion Swiss francs ($25.3 billion) in 1996 from 35.94 billion francs ($25.3 billion) in 1995. The two companies had a combined net profit in 1995 of 4.2 billion francs ($2.93 billion).

"Excluding one-off merger-related exceptional income and expenses, Novartis expects net income for the year as a whole to be approximately at the sale level as in the previous year...," Novartis said in a statement.
The group, based in Basle, Switzerland, expects to release its 1996 results on March 18.

Separately, the group said the scheduled spin-off of its Ciba Speciality Chemicals division is proceeding according to plan. It expects to list the unit on the Swiss stock exchange before the Novartis annual general meeting on April 22.
